Russian Roulette · A deduction game for six players

1. Setup and turn order
This is a solo game. Each player aims to maximize their own chance of survival. Each player receives a terminal and 16 credits. Seating is drawn by lot. The six-slot circular board holds 2 hidden elimination markers. The first seat leads Round 1. Actions proceed clockwise, and the lead seat moves one seat clockwise after each round. Before the first action and between credit actions, everyone can speak for free regardless of turn or balance. Everyone hears public remarks. A whisper goes only to one person seated beside the speaker. A recipient can reply once before the next credit action. Rotating the board does not change who sits next to whom.

2. Inspection and rotation
On your turn, choose one action you can afford. Public inspection costs 1 credit and private inspection costs 2. Each checks the selected slot and the next one for markers. Slot 1 follows slot 6. Everyone sees public inspection results. Only the player who inspects sees private results. Rotating by 1 slot costs 3 credits and rotating by 2 costs 4. The seat corresponding to slot 1 moves clockwise, and its new position is public.

3. Manipulation
Choose Manipulation to contribute 1–3 credits privately on your turn. When contributions reach 6 or more, the last contributor earns the right to swap the contents of two adjacent slots. The swap consumes all contributed credits, including any excess. The next Manipulation starts from 0. Other players only see that a private action occurred. Only the participant sees the contribution amount and swap positions.

4. Game end and survivors
Only you can see your credit balance during the game. If it reaches 0, you automatically skip later turns. The game ends after the action that reduces a third player's balance to 0. Starting at slot 1, check clockwise. The players assigned to the 2 marked slots are eliminated. The 4 survivors earn 1 Piece each.
